sections.title: Quadratic Equations Basics
sections.content: A quadratic equation is of the form ax² + bx + c = 0 (where a ≠ 0). The roots can be found using the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a.

sections.title: Discriminant & Nature of Roots
sections.content: The discriminant D = b² - 4ac determines root nature. If D > 0, roots are real and distinct. If D = 0, roots are real and equal. If D < 0, roots are imaginary/complex conjugates.

sections.title: Arithmetic Progression (AP)
sections.content: A sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is a constant (d). The nth term is Tn = a + (n-1)d. The sum of n terms is Sn = (n/2)[2a + (n-1)d] or (n/2)[a + l].

sections.title: Geometric Progression (GP)
sections.content: A sequence where the ratio of consecutive terms is a constant (r). The nth term is Tn = ar^(n-1). The sum of n terms is Sn = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1) for r ≠ 1.

sections.title: Harmonic Progression (HP)
sections.content: A sequence whose reciprocal terms form an Arithmetic Progression. Note: There is no general formula for the sum of an HP.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Applying the GP sum formula when r = 1.
2) Forgetting the ± sign when taking square roots.
3) Confusing the nth term (Tn) with the sum of n terms (Sn).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Quadratics deal with roots and discriminants. Sequences (AP/GP/HP) follow strict addition or multiplication patterns. Master the basic formulas first.

tricks.title: Sum and Product of Roots
tricks.explanation: Directly find them from the coefficients without calculating the roots.
tricks.example: For ax² + bx + c = 0, Sum (α+β) = -b/a, Product (αβ) = c/a.

tricks.title: Sum of First n Natural Numbers
Sum of First n Odd Numbers
tricks.explanation: The sum is always exactly n².

tricks.title: Sum of First n Even Numbers
Finding Common Difference Quickly
tricks.explanation: If Sn of an AP is given as a quadratic in n (An² + Bn), the common difference d is 2A.
